attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, endorsed. He re-quotes his earlier essay, but it is his own writing.

semantics.note: The normalisation rightly drops the hedged remark about what Dawkins believes and keeps the core point: saying human-like things does not show an LLM is like a person. It is a claim about an inference being invalid, which one counterexample can test.

contract.note: Scoring by counterexample is fair: human-like output produced by a different process shows the inference fails. The contract keeps this separate from any finding that models lack consciousness, which matches Marcus's narrower point.

evidence.note: Anthropic's 2025 interpretability write-up: Claude explains sums with the school carrying method, but internally it uses parallel approximate and exact paths. This meets the support condition. Caveat: it is a company disclosure about its own model, not an independent finding.

reviews.rationale: The contract's support condition is a documented case where a model's human-like explanation misdescribes its own processing. e1 gives one, dated before the cutoff. The packet has no evidence that similar language implies similar internal properties. e1 is a company disclosure, but it is primary mechanistic research and the finding cuts against the company's interest, so it counts as support with that caveat.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, re-quoted from his earlier essay inside his own post. Endorsed.

semantics.note: Faithful to the two-part contrast. 'Effectively', 'entire internet' and 'immense' are rhetorical and have no thresholds, which the contract flags.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: Marcus contrasts LLMs that memorise with humans who build models from experience, so evidence that LLMs learn structured representations bears on it. But how much memorisation counts, and what counts as a 'mental model', are evaluator choices, so the interpretation shapes the result.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed 2020 study: people learned abstract structure and transferred it to infer paths they had not seen. Supports the human model-building clause, within lab tasks.

Preprint dated January 2026, experiments run in 2025: production LLMs reproduced whole books nearly verbatim. Supports substantial memorisation, but not memorisation of the whole internet or memorisation as the account of all behaviour.

Llama-2 learns structured representations of space and time, which the authors call basic ingredients of a world model. This counts against treating LLMs as mere memorisers, though the authors hedge their conclusion.

reviews.rationale: The human clause holds (e1), and the memorisation claim holds in part (e2). The memorise-versus-model-build contrast is challenged by e3's structured representations in actual LLMs, which the contract counts as contradiction. Nothing in the packet measures how 'immense' the difference is. Mixed: the human clause and the memorisation component hold; the claim that LLMs only memorise does not.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Faithful, though 'interactive fiction' is a metaphor. In context ('NOT creating beings') it carries a denial that LLMs are experiencing beings, which the contract captures.

contract.note: Reading the claim as also denying genuine experience is fair given the context. That makes the result depend on questions about subjective experience, which the contract admits current evidence may not settle.

evidence.note: Shanahan et al. (2023): next-token training on human text, and dialogue agents as role-play 'all the way down'. This supports the training-and-simulation part, but the paper centres on base models and cautions that RL-tuned models may blur the distinction.

Butlin et al. (2023) tentatively find no current AI system conscious, using indicators drawn from theories of consciousness. The assessment is limited and dated 2023, so it does not settle the experience question for systems in May 2026.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports the training-and-role-play component (e1). It does not settle the stronger point that these systems are only fiction rather than experiencing beings: e1 hedges for RL-tuned models, e2 is limited context from 2023, and the packet's own stated gaps say subjective experience is unsettled. The support condition is therefore not met, and nothing meets the contradiction condition.
